questions_and_answers.question: What is the appropriate statistical test to assess whether there is an association between obesity status (normal weight, overweight, obese) and 5-year incident cardiovascular disease (CVD)? Suppose each participant’s obesity status (category) is known along with whether they develop CVD over the next 5 years or not.
questions_and_answers.answer: In the given question there are two variables - obesity status with three levels (normal, overweight, obese) and CVD status with two levels (developed CVD or not). To check whether these two variables have any association or not, the hypotheses are: H0:obesity status and CVD status are independent. HA: obesity status and CVD status are associated with each other. The appropriate test to test the claim is the Chi square test of independence as this test allows the researcher to know whether two categorical variables are related or not. Hence the answer is the Chi square test of independence.
